utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-95-17-I, the Prosecutor versus Miroslav Bralo. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I would like to let the parties remember that this hearing is held further to Article 62 of the Rules, Rule 62, in order to see the initial appearance of Mr. Bralo. Pursuant to the information which -- Bralo surrendered on the 10th of November 2004. The President of the Tribunal issued an order to begin the case -- assigning the case to Trial Chamber I, and therefore, I had to designate myself, since I was a member of the first Trial Chamber, to have this hearing for a first appearance, initial appearance of the accused. I would now like to ask the parties what are the appearances for the parties. Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. May it please the Court, Kenneth Scott, senior trial attorney appearing for the Prosecution, together with Mr. Fergal Gaynor, and our case manager, Mr. Sebastiaan van Hooydonk. I should indicate to the Court that this case is assigned to Mr. Mark Harmon, but Mr. Harmon is away from The Hague this week and I am covering for purposes of this appearance. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] thank you very much. Appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Virginia Lindsay on behalf of Mr. Miroslav Bralo. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, madam. Mr. Bralo, I would like to know if you can hear me in a language you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Are you indeed Miroslav Bralo?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] You also have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] What is this nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Cicko. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And you were born on the 13th of October, 1967?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Your Honour. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Kratine, Vitez municipality. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Very well. Before the armed conflict, you were working where? What was your job?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was working at the Zenica ironworks. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Were you not working at the Slobodan Princip Seljo plant?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, never. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] You are presently living at Nadioci?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And your height is about 1 metre, 90 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 184, in fact. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. You may sit down. I would now turn to the Prosecution to mention what is written in paragraph 8 of the indictment where it reads: [In English] "He worked in the Slobodan Princip Seljo factory." [Interpretation] And now Mr. Bralo tells us that he has never worked there. I would like to be told whether this information doesn't cast a doubt about the identity of Mr. Bralo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour Mr. President, I don't think I can shed any specific light on that point this afternoon. Mr. Bralo's answer comes as a bit of a surprise to me, to be perfectly honest. However, having said that, I have no reason to believe that that raises any serious issue as to his identification. I think in all other respects the accused has indicated that he is the person by this name, by this nickname, born at the location indicated, and a current living location. So -- JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Very well. I would also like to call your attention to the order which was made by Judge May on the 29th of January, which contains the following information - I will quote it; I've got a translation in French of this decision which says -- which reads: "He was a member of a military unit which was known under the name of the Jokers, and he measures 1 metre 90." Now Mr. Bralo is telling us that this is not exact and that his height is about -- well, it's within the measurement in question, but I want to be sure about the identity of the person in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, again, I would suggest that the differentiation, if you will, the discrepancy if one wants to call it that, in height is not so significant that it rules out that we have the right person here, and I suggest that based on what we know so far we do. As to his membership in a particular military unit, I might suggest, Your Honour, that that may take us further into what might be considered the merits of the case, and for purposes of identification I don't know that we would need to establish that at this moment. The Prosecution would submit that the difference in height between 184 metres -- approximately 184 centimetres, excuse me, and 190 is not so substantial as to raise a serious question. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] No, but at least it's a point on which I would like to have all the light shed as soon as possible, in order to be able to identify that it is indeed Mr. Bralo who is the accused person. Therefore, since you are on your feet, I would like to ask you to check the indictment at paragraph 3, first sentence, first line. Is there a typo when it mentioned HZ BZ armed forces? Did you mean HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, exactly correct. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Very well. So other the matters have -- will be checked. Minor detail. I would like you to have a look at page 5 and 6 of the indictment. Page 5 mentions a certain Victim B - this is in paragraph 23 - Victim B. Have you found the place? Can you follow me?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And page -- at page 6, in paragraph 24, it is said there is an accused, Accused B. Fourth line. And this indictment consists only of one indicted person, only one accused person. I'd like to remind you briefly the procedural history of this case. Initially there were four accused, if you remember that. Mr. Bralo was the first one of them. Number 2 was Mr. Furundzija who was tried by a Trial Chamber and by an Appeals Chamber, if I remember well, in July 2000. And as for the other two accused whose name I will not mention for the reason you know about, the indictment was withdrawn. Therefore, among four of the accused remains only Mr. Bralo who was concerned by this indictment which you call the service indictment -- the third indictment, filed on the 21st of December, 1998. May this perhaps cause also the Defence certain problems to know how this indictment was confirmed in November 1995? And now one reads here that the indictment was filed on the 21st of December, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll try to assist the Chamber as much as I can. The document that is dated on the front page of the document at the top, 21 December 1998, my understanding is that when this matter was considered by Judge May around that time, he had directed that a new version of the indictment be prepared for the purposes, indeed, of protecting the identity of certain persons. So when the indictment was prepared, this version which is the service copy, and it's my understanding the one that is dated 1998 on the top of the first page -- I am told is the version that has been served upon the accused, and that was the version that was specifically prepared at the direction of Judge May for purposes of protecting the identity of other persons in the indictment. But original indictment itself was returned and confirmed back in 1995 under the -- at the time when the Office of the Prosecutor was managed by Mr. Goldstone. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. On this occasion I would like also to draw your attention to -- without revealing, as far as the two other accused are concerned -- as far as one of them is concerned, the indictment was withdrawn on the 28th of May, 1998. As for the other accused, it was the 3rd of October, 2002. Therefore, until 2002, one of them at least was still accused. So a problem remains as far as -- well, concerning what you said, Accused B mentioned in paragraph 24 of the indictment, because we only have one accused, Mr. Bralo. This is what I understand. I see there might be a typo or some mistake. But when you say Accused B, who indeed is he? It's another accused person who doesn't feature in the indictment. I'm not asking you for an answer forthwith, but I would like to have, as soon as possible, an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I think -- I think I do know who Accused B is -- JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Anyway, please don't -- please go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At the Court's suggestion, and if the Court will allow, I would like to report that information after verifying and making sure of -- number one, that it's completely accurate; and number two, any concerns about protection that might still be in place. I don't think there are, but with the Court's permission, I would rather confirm that before making such a statement. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Therefore, this hearing, at this initial appearance, I have a duty to make sure that Mr. Bralo is properly informed about the indictment, against the accusations against him, levelled against him. I am sure the Defence knows that according to Articles -- Rule 62 of the Rules, a hearing has to take place to inform the accused, tell him what the indictment is about, and the accused has a right in 30 days to reflect, well -- his or her position and not to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty during that 30-day period; that the accused has a right to enter a plea during the initial appearance hearing if the accused so wishes. Therefore, Counsel, I would like to ask you whether you've made contact with Mr. Bralo and whether Mr. Bralo, first of all, has been informed by you of the general context of the indictment and whether you know whether Mr. Bralo intends to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty in this hearing, or whether the accused is asking for a deferral in -- which of course Rule 62 provides for. Yes, please, you can take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I've met with Mr. Bralo, and he has a general understanding of the charges against him, and he would ask that we have a further appearance scheduled in 30 days. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Counsel. This being said, I believe it is my duty to give a procedural history or, rather, a summary of the indictment. I will recall that the indictment contains four sections. The first section might be entitled "Facts," factual and temporal context of the indictment. In this section, the indictment speaks of the declaration of the independence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This section also deals with what was the position of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna, which considered itself as an independent political entity inside the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that as of January 1993 until mid-July 1993, armed forces of this community - these forces known as the Croatian Defence Council, the actual name HVO - were engaged in armed conflict with the armed forces of the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In this section, one can read also that as from the beginning of hostilities, the HVO forces attacked villages which were inhabited by Bosnian Muslims in the Lasva River Valley region, and the attacks resulted in the death and wounding of numerous civilians. In addition, other civilians were detained, transported from their places of residence, forced to perform manual labour. They were tortured, subjected to sexual assaults and other physical and mental abuse, physical and mental abuse. Hundreds of Bosnian Muslim civilians were arrested by the HVO forces and taken to the locations used as detention facilities. The indictment mentions two examples, the Vitez Cinema Complex; and secondly, the Vitez Veterinary Station, which were being used as detention facilities. In the indictment, one reads also that while imprisoned, numerous Bosnian Muslim prisoners were brought to the front lines where HVO soldiers forced them to dig protective trenches to protect HVO soldiers from being shot by BH snipers. One of these locations where the detainees were forced to dig trenches was at Kratine, a small hamlet in the Vitez municipality. After that, the indictment describes the accused himself, and mentions the fact that he was a member of a special forces group within the HVO called the Jokers, language -- Dzokeri in B/C/S. The third section of the indictment is entitled "General Allegations," bears the title "General Allegations," and I'd like to draw the attention of Defence counsel on this. The Prosecutor alleges in paragraph 9 - I quote in English: "At all times relevant to this indictment, a state of international armed conflict and partial occupation existed in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the territory of the former Yugoslavia." [Interpretation] I also recall that in the introduction of the indictment, there is a mention of an armed conflict between the forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but this conflict is not described or qualified in paragraph 3, [In English] "in an armed conflict." [Interpretation] But in the general allegations, Prosecution describes or qualifies the situation as being a conflict or - this is rather subtle - said that [In English] "armed conflict existed in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." [Interpretation] This being said, the indictment mentions in paragraph 14 in clear terms that these general allegations, general allegations contained in paragraph 9 through 14, are incorporated into each of the charges set forth in the indictment. The charges: There are 25 -- no, sorry, 21 charges. Yes, 21 charges, which are within the province of Rule 2 and 3 of the Tribunal's Statute, which is to say serious violations of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, as this is for Article 2 of the Statute, and Article 3, Laws and Customs of War. This roughly covers the indictment, corresponds to the indictment. Therefore, if Defence counsel wishes to ask any question at this stage, I invite you to take the floor if you want to discuss any matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. LINDSAY
utterances.text: I have no questions, Your Honour. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Does the Prosecution have any question to ask or any matter to discuss at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you very much. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. So I now invite the court deputy to give us a date -- fix a date within the next 30 coming days for a new opportunity given to Mr. Bralo to enter a plea on each count of the indictment and the crimes alleged. And before I adjourn this hearing, I would like to tell -- ask Mr. Bralo how his health is, whether he needs any treatment, any specific treatment or medical help. Mr. Bralo, may I hear you on this point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I'm entirely healthy. Thank you very much. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you so much. You can sit down. Therefore, I think we have no other business today and, therefore, the hearing is adjourned. Thank you very much.
